claims.text: Researchers at MD Anderson and collaborating Texas institutions developed an AI model that helps explain how immune cells reach specific places in the body and why they avoid others.
claims.quote: Researchers at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center and collaborating institutions in Texas developed an artificial intelligence (AI) model that helps explain how immune cells find their way to specific locations in the body and why they avoid others.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: The model is called SPACER. It reads spatial transcriptomics, a technique that measures gene activity in intact tissue and shows which genes are expressed and where.
claims.quote: The tool, known as Spatial Analysis of Cellular Engagement and Recruitment (SPACER), makes use of spatial transcriptomics, a molecular technique that measures gene activity within intact tissue to highlight which genes are expressed and where.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: SPACER looks at groups of neighboring cells and how they work together rather than at each cell alone.
claims.quote: Instead of treating cells as isolated units, the tool examines groups of neighboring cells and how they work together.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: The team ran SPACER on 37 datasets and reports it was four to 21 times more effective than existing approaches in benchmarking tasks.
claims.quote: The team applied SPACER across 37 datasets representing several cancer types. In benchmarking tasks, the model was four- to 21-times more effective than existing approaches at identifying biologically meaningful signals linked to cell recruitment.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away
claims.note: The benchmark figure is the researchers' own result. The journal abstract (c20) states the same range and says the 37 datasets include mouse heart as well as human tumor types.

claims.text: Immune cells appear to respond mainly to signals close by rather than to signals circulating elsewhere in the body.
claims.quote: One of the most meaningful findings was that immune cells appear to respond primarily to signals in their immediate surroundings rather than signals circulating elsewhere in the body.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: Tumors expressing genes for antigen presentation were more likely to attract T cells. Antigen presentation is how cells display protein fragments for immune cells to inspect.
claims.quote: SPACER revealed that tumors expressing genes involved in antigen presentation, the process by which cells display protein fragments for immune cells to inspect, were more likely to attract T cells.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: Mucins are large sugar coated proteins made by many cancers. The researchers found evidence they may help form physical barriers that keep T cells away from tumors.
claims.quote: Additionally, the researchers uncovered evidence that mucins, a family of large, sugar-coated proteins produced by many cancers, may help create physical barriers that keep T cells away from tumors.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: In several melanoma and gastric cancer datasets, tumors with more mucin were associated with poorer responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors and poorer patient outcomes.
claims.quote: Across several melanoma and gastric cancer datasets, tumors with higher levels of mucins were associated with poorer responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors and poorer patient outcomes.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away
claims.note: An association in existing datasets. The release reports no use in patient care.

claims.text: The researchers believe SPACER could potentially serve as a diagnostic tool for cancer therapies. The release presents this as a possibility and reports no such use.
claims.quote: The researchers believe SPACER could potentially be used as a diagnostic tool for cancer therapies and to improve understanding of diseases and scenarios in which cell movement and positioning are important, including autoimmune disorders, tissue repair and wound healing.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: Linghua Wang says SPACER turns its insights into new ideas the team can test in the lab.
claims.quote: This helps us turn these insights into new ideas we can test in the lab.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away
claims.note: The sentence closes a quotation paragraph attributed to Linghua Wang.

claims.text: The study was published in Nature Biomedical Engineering and co-led by Tao Wang and Linghua Wang. Tao Wang is an associate professor of Bioinformatics and Computational Biology. Linghua Wang is a professor of Genomic Medicine.
claims.quote: The study, published in Nature Biomedical Engineering , was co-led by Tao Wang, Ph.D. , associate professor of Bioinformatics and Computational Biology ; and Linghua Wang, M.D., Ph.D. , professor of Genomic Medicine
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away
claims.note: The record's string keeps the spaces the page's link markup leaves in its extracted text.

claims.text: MD Anderson says the study was funded in part by the National Institutes of Health, the Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas and the U.S. Department of Defense, along with a foundation and a Baylor College of Medicine seed grant.
claims.quote: This study was funded in part by the National Institutes of Health, the Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas, the U.S. Department of Defense, the Adrienne Helis Malvin Medical Research Foundation, and a Baylor College of Medicine Department of Surgery Seed Grant.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: Linghua Wang leads the Center for Cellular Language Intelligence at MD Anderson as its executive director and head.
claims.quote: executive director and head of the Center for Cellular Language Intelligence
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: Applied to data from preclinical models of heart inflammation caused by immunotherapy, SPACER identified heart regions and molecular signals associated with T cell recruitment.
claims.quote: Interestingly, applying SPACER to data from preclinical models of immunotherapy-related myocarditis, or heart inflammation, identified regions of the heart and molecular signals associated with T cell recruitment.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: In those preclinical models the tool suggested CD4 positive T cells may play a larger role in severe heart inflammation than previously recognized.
claims.quote: The tool suggested that CD4-positive T cells may play a larger role in driving severe heart inflammation than previously recognized.
claims.document: MD Anderson research news release, AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away

claims.text: The journal article is titled Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues.
claims.quote: Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues
claims.document: Nature Biomedical Engineering article page, Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues

claims.text: Nature Biomedical Engineering published the article on October 13th, 2026.
claims.quote: Published: 13 October 2026
claims.document: Nature Biomedical Engineering article page, Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues

claims.text: The abstract describes SPACER as a fully interpretable learning framework that decodes gene level recruitment rules from spatially resolved transcriptomics data.
claims.quote: Here we introduce SPACER, a fully interpretable multi-instance learning framework that decodes gene-level recruitment rules
claims.document: Nature Biomedical Engineering article page, Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues

claims.text: The abstract says existing tools for spatially resolved transcriptomics describe where cells sit and can't explain why.
claims.quote: Existing computational tools for spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) describe where cells reside but cannot explain
claims.document: Nature Biomedical Engineering article page, Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues

claims.text: The journal abstract says the 37 datasets span multiple human tumor types and mouse heart, and puts the improvement over existing methods at 4 to 21 fold.
claims.quote: Applied to 37 SRT datasets spanning multiple human tumour types and mouse heart, SPACER achieved 4–21-fold improvement over existing methods
claims.document: Nature Biomedical Engineering article page, Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues
claims.note: The page's own character between 4 and 21 is an en dash, kept in the quote. No published string reproduces it.

claims.text: The abstract says tumor mucins are associated with physical barriers to T cell engagement, which predicts resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors and patient prognosis.
claims.quote: SPACER revealed (1) that tumour-expressed mucins are associated with physical barriers to T cell engagement, which predicts resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors and patient prognosis
claims.document: Nature Biomedical Engineering article page, Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues
claims.note: Read as two exact consecutive fragments joined at the comma after engagement.

claims.text: The National Cancer Institute says immune checkpoint inhibitors work by blocking checkpoint proteins from binding with their partner proteins.
claims.quote: Immunotherapy drugs called immune checkpoint inhibitors work by blocking checkpoint proteins from binding with their partner proteins.
claims.document: National Cancer Institute, Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors
claims.note: The page shows Reviewed April 7, 2022 and no publication date.

claims.text: The National Cancer Institute dictionary says that when these checkpoints are blocked, T cells can kill cancer cells better.
claims.quote: When these checkpoints are blocked, T cells can kill cancer cells better.
claims.document: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, immune checkpoint inhibitor

claims.text: The National Cancer Institute dictionary defines a T cell as a type of white blood cell that is part of the immune system.
claims.quote: A type of white blood cell. T cells are part of the immune system
claims.document: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, T cell

claims.text: The National Cancer Institute dictionary describes mucin as the main compound in mucus.
claims.quote: Containing or resembling mucin, the main compound in mucus.
claims.document: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, mucinous
claims.note: The dictionary's entry for mucinous. It has no entry for mucin alone.

rejected.finding: CPRIT is a state agency Texas voters approved, with a stated authorization to award a dollar amount
rejected.reason: cprit.texas.gov answered 403 to the fetcher on four urls, and the constitutional text served only navigation. No voter approval sentence or figure was read. The only CPRIT fact carried is that the release names it as a funder (c12).

rejected.finding: An NCI dictionary definition of mucin alone
rejected.reason: The NCI glossary has no entry for mucin. The mucinous entry is carried as c25 and labelled as that entry.

rejected.finding: Tao Wang and Linghua Wang as the paper's lead or senior authors from the journal page
rejected.reason: The journal page lists Jia Yao first and Tao Wang last and states no co-lead role. Co-led is MD Anderson's description and is carried only as the release's words in c11.

rejected.finding: A release date claim quoting the release's dateline
rejected.reason: The dateline may be assembled from separate page elements, so it is not carried as a quote. October 13th sits in the published field, and the journal's own date is verified in c17.
